00:10.000–00:11.000 — Voice continues: “Now when a fire burns, it does so with the help of firewood.”

00:11.000–00:12.000 — Voice continues: “When a fire is burning, if someone were to ask us, ‘What is burning? What shall we say as a reply?’”

00:12.000–00:13.000 — Voice continues: “Is it the wood that is burning, or the fire that is burning?”

00:14.000–00:15.000 — Voice continues: “So it seems we already have here a case of relatedness of this to that, ida-paccayata.”

00:15.000–00:16.000 — Voice continues: “This itself shows that there is a very deep significance in the fire simile.”

00:03.000–00:05.000: A female voice begins speaking, clear and natural, with no noticeable reverb or echo. She says: “Why don’t I see Nirvana right now?”

00:05.000–00:06.000: A brief pause. No speech.

00:06.000–00:13.000: A male voice begins speaking, calm and measured, with a slightly resonant quality. He says: “You do not see Nirvana right now because you imagine a seer and a world, and neither is there.”

00:13.000–00:14.000: A brief pause. No speech.

00:14.000–00:22.000: The same male voice continues: “What is called manana is the imagining in egoistic terms, imparting reality to illusory things.”

00:22.000–00:23.000: A brief pause. No speech.

00:23.000–00:30.000: The male voice continues: “Only looking is there, nothing worth looking at. Only a seeing is there, nothing to be seen.”

00:30.000–00:31.000: A brief pause. No speech.

00:31.000–00:38.000: The male voice continues: “The law of dependent arising is already implicated. There is therefore no seer apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathagata.”

00:38.000–00:39.000: A brief pause. No speech.

00:39.000–00:46.000: The male voice continues: “Samsara is a whirlpool as far as the ordinary beings caught up in it are concerned.”

00:46.000–00:47.000: A brief pause. No speech.

00:47.000–00:52.000: The male voice continues: “Now what about the arhants? How is the idea of this whirlpool presented in the case of the arhants?”

00:52.000–00:53.000: A brief pause. No speech.

00:53.000–00:58.000: The male voice continues: “It is simply said that for them there is no whirling round for there to be a designation.”

00:58.000–00:59.000: A brief pause. No speech.

00:59.000–01:04.000: The male voice continues: “Pattam te sam natti panna panaya. So in their case, there is no whirling round to justify a designation.”
